review_notes: I read all 49 lines. The file has four plain defs (gaussian3, polyGauss3, godementInner3, jacquetIntegrand3, jacquetVector3), one membership theorem proved by `funext M; simp`, and one rfl unfolding lemma, jacquetVector3_eq. None of the declarations carries a simp attribute, so there are no competing rules, no orientation problem and no loop risk. I grepped the repo for uses. jacquetVector3_eq is used through explicit `rw` (e.g. `rw [Phi, jacquetVector3_eq, ...realMat_one, Matrix.det_one]`), and the definitions are unfolded with `simp [jacquetIntegrand3, ...]` where needed. That is a reasonable interface, and making the definitions `@[simp]` would risk unwanted expansion of the integrals. I found no concrete simp-interface defect that I could support from the sources. The only uncertainty is that I did not inspect every downstream proof, since some of them are very large.
